A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReStraV research. Their text, equations, tables, scientific figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite appendix repagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original classifier and benchmark results in Sections 6–7, together with feature-importance, sampling-ablation, and scene-cut analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including detection benchmarks, matched-video evaluations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Both retain frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 embeddings, curvature and stepwise-distance features, the 21-dimensional classifier input, the same lightweight classifiers, and the Physics-IQ curvature-based decision rule.

E1.justification: Both cover VidProM/DVSC2023, GenVidBench Main and Plants tasks, DeMamba one-to-many evaluation, Veo3 zero-shot detection, and matched Physics-IQ pairs. Generator populations and appendix test scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Classifier comparisons, baseline membership in Tables 2–5, and the Gemini 1.5 Pro comparison are unchanged. Correcting the VideoSwin citation from the TALL reference to the Video Swin reference does not change the evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample sizes, preprocessing, frame sampling, classifier configurations, metrics, timing procedures, and two-alternative forced-choice evaluation remain unchanged. Appendices B–C retain the same experimental settings.

E4.justification: Appendices A–C retain the classifier analyses, permutation feature importance, qualitative examples, video-length and sampling-density ablations, window-position robustness test, and scene-cut analysis. Relocation adds no new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Section 5 retains the same statistical tests. Appendix B still reports multiple runs with different samples and splits and shading of one standard deviation; Figure 11 retains standard-deviation error bars. No new seed or run-count information is provided.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the scientific figures retain their results. For example, Table 1 still reports MLP accuracy of 94.17% and AUROC of 98.63%, and the Veo3 test remains at 83.2% accuracy. Appendix curves, confusion matrices, and scene-cut values also match.

T1.justification: The displacement, distance, and curvature definitions in Section 3 and Equation (1), and the statistical-feature formulas in Section 5, are unchanged. Neither version contains additional appendix proofs or formal developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and discussion summary retain the same claims about geometric detection signals, computational efficiency, competitive performance, and generalization. No contribution is added, removed, or substantively redefined.

C2.justification: Both retain the differential-straightening explanation, curvature-variance interpretation, neuroscience implications, and appendix interpretations. Time-reversal invariance, adversarial adaptation, future-generator limitations, and encoder-bias concerns are also unchanged.

D1.justification: The code disclosure, implementation and classifier details, Appendix D hardware and timing information, and Appendix E dataset sources and licenses are retained. Bibliographic updates do not introduce new implementation or resource-access instructions.

R1.justification: There are limited changes to cited works: the Westerlund reference is replaced by van der Sloot and Wagensveld, and v2's broader-impact references 87–88 are removed. The research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix A remains unchanged; most other reference edits concern metadata.

P1.justification: v4 corrects David Klindt's name, adds an illustration credit, makes a small wording edit, and revises bibliographic metadata and formatting. The main narrative, section order, and appendix prose remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds an unnumbered illustration beneath Appendix Contents and changes appendix figure placement. For example, Figures 15–16 now share a page. Existing scientific graphics and table designs are retained, with no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves attribution and reference completeness: Section 7B/Table 3 now cites Video Swin instead of TALL, and VideoCrafter and Stable Video Diffusion entries replace literal placeholder identifiers with specified references. These are useful editorial gains; the method, empirical evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
